inventory.name: text-decoration-skip-spaces — the CSS property that controls whether text decoration lines (underline, overline, line-through) skip spacers and word separators

syntax.rationale: The anchored slice carries the declaration shape as an author writes it, in semantic <code> inside a <pre><code> rule block: `.skip-spaces { text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-skip-spaces: all; }` and `.no-skip { text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-skip-spaces: none; }`, i.e. the property name, two of its keywords, and the companion `text-decoration` declaration the property modifies. GAP FLAGGED, NOT PAPERED OVER: the full propdef — css-text-decor-4 §2.10.3 grammar `none | all | [ start || end ]`, Initial `start end`, Applies to all elements, Inherited yes, Computed value specified keyword(s), Animation type discrete — sits in the page's UN-ANCHORED 'the property' and 'Values' tables, which this unit's three canonical ids do not reach (see notes for why #syntax sits on 'live demo'). DIVERGENCE REPORTED, NOT FIXED: the page's Values table documents the keywords `leading` and `trailing`, which §2.10.3 does not define; the spec keywords are `start` and `end`, and WPT css/css-text-decor/text-decoration-skip-spaces-001.html and -002.html both declare `text-decoration-skip-spaces: start end`.

inputs.rationale: The inputs to this surface are declarative and the anchored slice carries two of them in <code>: the keyword written on the declaration (`all`, `none`) and the selector the declaration is written for, with each keyword's rendered effect shown beside it. GAP FLAGGED, NOT PAPERED OVER: the slice shows two of the spec's four keywords — `start` and `end` (§2.10.3 grammar `none | all | [ start || end ]`, where start and end combine) appear only in the UN-ANCHORED 'Values' table, and that table spells them `leading`/`trailing`, keywords the spec does not define; nor does any anchored fragment carry the Initial value (`start end` per the propdef) or the 'spacer' definition (any Unicode General Category Zs typographic character unit except U+202F NARROW NO-BREAK SPACE, plus adjacent letter-spacing/word-spacing for all/start/end). Both are reported as divergences and gaps, not written into the page.

outputs.rationale: The output is a rendering change and the anchored slice shows it twice: two live rows under the same phrase, one with `all` ('each word underlined separately', gaps at the word boundaries) and one with `none` ('continuous underline across spaces'), plus the <pre><code> rules that produce them. Per §2.10.3 the specified effect is that spacers and word separators (plus any adjacent letter-spacing or word-spacing) are not painted under, and the property controls all decoration lines drawn by the element as well as any drawn by its ancestors. A CSS property returns no script-visible value, so the painted result is the whole output surface.

errors.rationale: A declarative CSS property has no exception, rejection or error-code surface: there is no call to fail, so nothing throws and the anchored slice documents no error path. The only failure mode is availability — a browser without the property, or a keyword it does not support, drops the declaration at parse time per standard CSS error handling and paints the decoration as if the declaration were absent. GAP FLAGGED: the page states that dropped-declaration fallback nowhere, and the ChromeStatus record's activation_risks field is null, so neither cited source describes the degradation path either.

context.rationale: Exposure and prerequisites are carried by the anchored support table: Chrome '150 — developer trial (flag required)', Edge 'Tracking Chromium', Firefox 'No signal', Safari 'No signal'. Verified against the record on 2026-10-07 — DevTrial stage_type 230 desktop_first/android_first 150 and flag_name 'enable-experimental-web-platform-features' — so the flag-gated developer-trial prerequisite that cell states is the record's own value, and ff_views 5 / safari_views 5 decode to 'No signal'. GAP FLAGGED, NOT PAPERED OVER: the flag's own URL (chrome://flags/#enable-experimental-web-platform-features, in the page's un-anchored warn-block and at-a-glance table) and the element scope (Applies to: all elements; Inherited: yes, in the un-anchored 'the property' table) are outside every anchored fragment.

lifecycle.rationale: An inherited declarative property has no runtime lifecycle: nothing is constructed, registered, awaited, cancelled or torn down, and its effect is recomputed at each style, layout and paint pass rather than moving through states of its own. The only transitions this page documents are release-availability ones — the anchored table's developer trial in Chrome 150, with the record's Ship stage_type 260 at desktop/android/webview 155 — which belong to the context and compatibility dimensions above, not to a lifecycle of the property.

examples.rationale: The anchored slice carries one complete semantic <pre><code> example — two rules, `.skip-spaces` with `text-decoration-skip-spaces: all` and `.no-skip` with `none`, each beside the `text-decoration: underline` it modifies — plus two rendered rows showing the visual difference, which is what the example claims. The sibling 'recipes' section adds two further <pre><code> rules (link underlines with text-underline-offset and text-decoration-skip-ink; a line-through sale price); it is deliberately NOT anchored, because an id on that <h2> would resolve to an empty fragment (fragmentAfterId() stops at its first <h3>).

compatibility.rationale: Tabular per-engine support, including explicit unknowns: Chrome '150 — developer trial (flag required)', Edge 'Tracking Chromium', Firefox 'No signal', Safari 'No signal', cited to 'chromestatus browser views, May 2026'. Checked against the record on 2026-10-07: DevTrial stage desktop_first/android_first 150, ff_views 5 and safari_views 5 = 'No signal', browsers.chrome.status.text 'Proposed'. UNSOURCED CELL REPORTED, NOT ADJUDICATED: the record carries no Edge-specific field, so 'Tracking Chromium' is Chromium-parity inference rather than a value in the cited source. OMISSION REPORTED: the record's Ship stage (desktop/android/webview 155) is a milestone the table does not mention.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The property changes only where decoration lines are painted across spacers and word separators: it exposes no data, grants no capability, and adds no script-visible state, storage, permission, network or cross-origin surface, and the anchored slice shows nothing but that painting difference. css-text-decor-4's own Privacy Considerations section reads 'No new privacy considerations have been reported on this specification' and its Security Considerations section reads 'No new security considerations have been reported on this specification' (fetched 2026-10-07). NOT CORROBORATED BY THE RECORD, stated rather than smoothed over: ChromeStatus 4832783806627840 carries security_review_status 'Pending' and privacy_review_status 'Pending', so what the record says is that the reviews are unfinished, not that the feature was found clean.
